issues.description: RPC inlines full script content instead of exposing it as a separately addressable resource.
issues.detail: compile_notebook silently broadened its contract to ship arbitrary-size file content alongside the path that already identifies the artifact. Every compile pays for a full file read regardless of whether anyone downloads. Strip script_content from the RPC and add a dedicated read/serve endpoint keyed by path, so identity and value are decoupled and downloads are on-demand.

issues.description: Script content is threaded through React state and re-materialized as a Blob when a path would suffice.
issues.detail: compiledContent flows through DeploysProgress state, props, and DeployProgress purely to build a Blob and object URL for click-time download. The server already wrote the file; a plain anchor against a served URL avoids holding the artifact in two memory representations and removes Blob/objectURL lifecycle complexity entirely.

issues.description: DeployProgress complects progress rendering with file-download mechanics.
issues.detail: handleDownloadClick embeds Blob construction, object URLs, DOM mutation, and revoke lifecycle inside a component whose contract is rendering deploy state. Extract a downloadFile(name, content) utility (or use a declarative <a download href>) so the component stays focused and the download mechanism is independently testable.

issues.description: File is opened without explicit encoding or size bound.
issues.detail: open(script_path) uses the platform default encoding and reads the entire file unconditionally, leaking platform behavior through the RPC postcondition. Specify encoding='utf-8' and state (or enforce) a size cap so the returned string has a stable contract independent of the server's locale and the payload cannot grow unboundedly.

issues.description: Download affordance precondition is not enforced at the type level.
issues.detail: The icon renders unconditionally in the success branch but handleDownloadClick guards on both compiledPath and compiledContent, so a missing value yields a silent no-op for the user. Either make compiledContent required by the branch's type or hide the icon when it is absent, so the affordance and its precondition agree.

issues.description: Download control is an onClick icon, inconsistent with its anchor neighbor and not keyboard-reachable.
issues.detail: GetAppIcon with onClick sits next to a real anchor that already uses the browser's native download behavior. Make it an <a download href> (or a real <button>) so the control is keyboard-accessible and consistent with the adjacent affordance. This falls out naturally if the backend exposes a served URL.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees the feature is useful but the data shape is wrong: compile_notebook silently broadened its contract to inline the entire compiled script, and that content is then threaded through three layers of React state to be re-materialized as a Blob at click time — when a path already exists. Consensus fix is to strip script_content from the RPC, expose a dedicated read/serve endpoint, and let a plain anchor handle the download. Secondary cleanups: extract download mechanics out of DeployProgress, specify utf-8 encoding (and a size bound) on the file read, and tie the icon's visibility to its precondition while making it keyboard-accessible.
